\boxed{(h_*,W_*)=\left(\frac32,\frac18\right)}

Let \(x_*=0\), \(f_*=0\), \(\|x_0\|\le 1\), and write
\[
g=\nabla f(x_0),\qquad x_1=x_0-\frac32 g,\qquad q=\nabla f(x_1).
\]

For any convex \(1\)-smooth differentiable \(f\), the interpolation inequality gives
\[
f(u)\ge f(v)+\nabla f(v)\cdot(u-v)+\frac12\|\nabla f(u)-\nabla f(v)\|^2.
\]
Using it between \(x_0,x_1\) and the minimizer gives
\[
f(x_1)\le g\cdot x_0-\|g\|^2-\frac12 q\cdot g-\frac12\|q\|^2,
\]
and also
\[
f(x_1)\le q\cdot x_0-\frac32 q\cdot g-\frac12\|q\|^2.
\]
Averaging these two bounds,
\[
f(x_1)\le \frac12(g+q)\cdot x_0-\frac12\|g+q\|^2.
\]
Let \(v=(g+q)/2\). Since \(\|x_0\|\le1\),
\[
f(x_1)\le v\cdot x_0-2\|v\|^2
\le \|v\|-2\|v\|^2
\le \frac18.
\]
Thus \(W(3/2)\le 1/8\).

This is sharp. In one dimension, take
\[
f(t)=\int_0^t \min(\max(s,0),1/4)\,ds,
\]
with \(x_0=1\). Then \(g=1/4\), so for \(h=3/2\),
\[
x_1=1-\frac32\cdot\frac14=\frac58,
\]
and
\[
f(x_1)=\frac18.
\]
Hence \(W(3/2)=1/8\).

To see uniqueness, two one-dimensional examples give, for every \(h>0\),
\[
W(h)\ge \frac1{2(2h+1)}
\]
from the clipped-gradient construction with \(g=1/(2h+1)\), and
\[
W(h)\ge \frac12(h-1)^2
\]
from \(f(t)=t^2/2\), \(x_0=1\). Therefore
\[
W(h)\ge \max\left\{\frac1{2(2h+1)},\frac12(h-1)^2\right\}.
\]
This lower bound is \(>1/8\) for every \(h\ne3/2\), while at \(h=3/2\) it equals \(1/8\). So the unique minimizer is \(h_*=3/2\), with \(W_*=1/8\).
